title: Secrets Project
summary: End-of-module project: a small Express + EJS site (called Lisper) that calls the Secrets API /random endpoint with Axios and shows a random anonymous secret and its username on a styled card. No authentication is used, keeping the focus on consuming an API from a server.

concepts.heading: Project overview
points: A server-rendered site inspired by the anonymous-confession app Whisper. Each page load shows one random user's name; the secret text is revealed when hovering over the card (hover effect is already in the supplied CSS).
Only the /random endpoint of the Secrets API is used, so no bearer token, registration or login is needed.
Skills practised: Express routing and static files, EJS templating with variables, reading API docs, and using Axios with async/await.

Starting files: index.js with numbered hint comments, solution.js (finished version), views/index.ejs, public/styles/main.css and an image. The CSS can be replaced if the learner wants their own design.

concepts.heading: Template contract with EJS
points: index.ejs expects exactly two variables: secret (printed inside the card paragraph with the escaping tag) and user (printed in a paragraph with class user).
The stylesheet is linked as styles/main.css, which only resolves because public is served as a static folder (the public part of the path is omitted in the URL).

concepts.heading: Server walkthrough (the six hints)
points: 1. Import express and axios (both are listed in package.json dependencies; run npm i first).
2. Create the app with express() and set port 3000.
3. app.use(express.static('public')) is built-in Express middleware that serves files from the named folder, so stylesheets and images can be requested relative to it.
4. Define app.get('/') as the home route.

5. Inside the handler, await axios.get on the /random URL. The URL can be written in full or split into a base URL and config; Axios methods return promises, so either chain .then() or make the handler async and use await.

The response body is at result.data and contains id, secret, emScore and username. Map the API keys to the template variable names: secret from result.data.secret, user from result.data.username. Logging result.data is a good way to confirm the keys.

Wrap the call in try/catch. In the catch block, log error.response.data for the developer (the message from the API) and respond with HTTP status 500 plus a generic message for visitors instead of exposing details.
6. app.listen(port, callback) with a console message such as server started on port 3000.
Run with nodemon index.js and visit localhost:3000; refreshing the page fetches a different random secret.

concepts.heading: API caveat
points: The Secrets API is a teaching service, not production infrastructure. User data (registrations, tokens, secrets) is wiped regularly, roughly every day or two, so it should not be relied on for a real product.
The next section uses more robust public APIs suitable for portfolio projects.

task.name: Secrets Project (Lisper)
task.starting_point: Extracted project with index.js containing six hint comments, a finished views/index.ejs, public/styles/main.css and an image. solution.js runs the completed app.
task.goal: Build an Express server that fetches a random secret from the Secrets API and renders its text and username into index.ejs.
steps: cd into the project folder and run npm i.
Optionally run nodemon solution.js and open localhost:3000 to see the target behaviour.
Read index.ejs to learn the two variables it needs: secret and user.
In index.js import express and axios, create the app, set port 3000.
Serve the public folder with express.static.
Add an async GET / route that awaits axios.get('https://secrets-api.appbrewery.com/random').
Render index.ejs passing secret: result.data.secret and user: result.data.username.
Add try/catch: log error.response.data and send a 500 with a friendly message.
Call app.listen with a log message, run nodemon index.js and refresh to see random secrets. Optionally extend the project.
task.expected_result: A styled card showing a username; hovering reveals the secret. Each refresh shows a different random entry.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 28 - Aplication Programming Interfaces (APIs)/28.07 - Secrets Project/solution.js

pitfalls: Template variable names (secret, user) must match the keys passed to res.render; the API field is username, not user, so it needs mapping.
Forgetting express.static means the CSS and image return 404.
Forgetting await leaves result as a pending promise and result.data is undefined.
The reference repo's catch block only calls res.status(500) without sending anything, so the browser request hangs; add .send(...) (the lecture describes showing a message).
(Extra) error.response is undefined on network failures, so logging error.response.data can itself throw; log error.message as a fallback.

gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson: 'Random secret viewer'. Blurb: call a single public GET endpoint from Express and render the fields into a template.
Tasks: (1) set up express + static folder; (2) await axios.get on /random; (3) pass selected fields to the template; (4) add try/catch with a 500 response; (5) extend by showing emScore.
Starter code idea: server skeleton with the six hint comments and a mock fetch function standing in for Axios.
Interactive demo idea: a fake API response viewer where learners click which JSON keys to map to template variables and see the rendered card update.
